prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Explore Adoption Pathways", "Preview how adopting a ready pet or creating a custom pet works before deciding."]
1: ["Pet Customization Studio", "Upload photos to generate your unique desktop companion.", "Select Photos"]
2: ["How to Interact with Your Pet", "Learn quick desktop shortcuts to chat with, move, or temporarily hide your pet."]
3: []
4: ["Signing in anchors your pet to your account so it is never lost or reset.", "Cloud Pet Preservation Active"]
5: ["Generating Your Desktop Companion", "Configuring desktop graphics and mascot behaviors..."]
6: ["Choose How You Adopt", "Select between instant premade pet adoption or custom photo generation."]
7: ["Official Pet Adoption Certificate", "Name your companion to register it for immediate desktop launch.", "Your companion will appear directly on your screen upon completion."]
8: ["Your Pet Has Arrived!", "Setup complete! You've unlocked a complimentary desktop starter toy for your pet.", "Reward Unlocked: Desktop Starter Toy"]
9: ["Feel free to minimize the app; we will ping you as soon as your pet lands on screen."]
